newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends a bit lower after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends a bit lower after quiet day.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended a shade weaker in thin dealings Monday, as speculative selling kept the market under pressure, trading sources said.
Scale-down trade buying stemmed the losses, they said, preventing a test of key chart support at 10.29 cents.
The market probed the upside early on, bolstered by a bout of commercial buying. But speculators proved ready sellers above 10.40 cents basis March, prompting a quick retracement toward the lows.
Benchmark March eased 0.01 on the day to 10.35 after trading from 10.30 to 10.45. Second-position May slipped 0.04 to 10.42 while outer months fell between 0.03 and 0.05 cent.
The day's turnover was muted, at an estimated 8,702 lots.

Traders said March's ability to hold 10.29 cents, an intraday low from last Thursday and Friday, should offer some marginal support. But they cautioned that with end-users keeping a lid on their buying, any upside progress would be difficult.
"There is plenty of sugar around, and little off-take," said one dealer. "Russia and China are not buying much."
On the charts, 10.21-10.20 cents would be a key downside target if 10.29 were breached. To shore up its outlook, March would need to clear 10.45-10.50 cents, traders said.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
